business_ops.seasonality: Business is subject to seasonality. Merchants have historically experienced lower demand for their products on their direct sales channels (websites and apps) in the THIRD QUARTER of each Fiscal, during the Diwali festivities, largely because more sales and discounts are offered on large e-commerce marketplaces, which reduces demand for products supplied by Merchants on their direct sales channels. As a result the Company has historically generated lower revenues in its third quarter than in other quarters. The RHP cautions that its limited operating history makes the exact nature of the impact difficult to judge and that the business may become MORE seasonal as Merchant solutions offerings grow. No quarterly revenue figures are printed to quantify the effect.

COURIER-PARTNER CONCENTRATION (separate table): 42 active courier partners as of March 31, 2026; shipments by the top five active couriers 149.13 / 121.86 / 94.34 million and their share of TOTAL SHIPMENT VOLUMES 84.50% / 83.33% / 83.38% in Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024 - i.e. courier concentration WORSENED in Fiscal 2026 to its three-year high. Total shipment volume is not printed as an absolute number and has not been derived. No exclusive arrangements with logistics partners; contracts are on an independent-contractor basis, typically long-term and open-ended until terminated.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Asset-light aggregator / platform model with no backward or forward integration into physical logistics: the Company owns no delivery fleets and no fulfilment centres, and operates entirely out of leased premises and co-working spaces. Third-party logistics partners (42 active courier partners as of March 31, 2026), fulfilment centre providers, communication platforms, shopping carts, marketplaces, payment gateways, ERPs, developers and credit providers are integrated via APIs into an ecosystem of more than 250 partners from April 2021 to March 2026. Contracts with logistics partners are on an independent-contractor, non-exclusive basis, typically long-term and remaining in force until terminated by either side, with standard pricing by weight and delivery area plus insurance and indemnity provisions. Despite the outsourced supply, the Company runs a 'full-responsibility model', taking complete ownership of platform transactions from fulfilment to payments and post-order processes, including escalating complaints, handling operational lapses and absorbing financial losses arising from shipments; COD remittance to Merchants runs on a cycle independent of the logistics providers' own remittance process. Forward extensions are software-led rather than physical: Fastrr Checkout at the front of the order journey, Engage360/ads at demand generation, Shiprocket Fintech (13 NBFC and lending partners in Fiscal 2026, bilateral lending directly between partner and Merchant) for working capital, and Shiprocket Quick as an aggregator-model hyperlocal layer. Physical footprint is limited to 13 leased fulfilment centres (762,826 sq ft across 10 cities), warehouse management at 5 customer-owned fulfilment centres and 11 third-party-operated warehouses. Inorganic build-out rather than integration: Glaucus (February 2022), Pickrr (June 2022, fully integrated in Fiscal 2024), Shiprocket Omuni (October 2022) and Swiftly/Wigzo (December 2021, marketing-automation tool acquired September 2023 and stake sold); goodwill impairments of ₹1,246.41 million (Shiprocket Omuni) and ₹521.01 million (Swiftly/Wigzo) were taken as exceptional items in Fiscal 2024. In Fiscal 2026 the Company made an investment in a company providing storage, warehousing and logistics services.

opportunities: Strategy - retain and grow the Merchant base by expanding product offerings addressing Merchant challenges in payments, capital, shipping and fulfilment, and cross-selling existing and new products to improve unit economics, margins and ARPU.
Strategy - invest in the Emerging Business to unlock growth for Merchants' businesses and expand the Company's total addressable market.

Strategy - strengthen the ecosystem by growing the ecosystem network and through inorganic growth, adding integrations with payment gateways, loyalty providers, shopping carts, ERP platforms, shipping partners, marketing solution providers and lenders; participation in ONDC as both a logistics network participant and a seller app.

Self-serve platform offering enterprise-grade experience drawing organic traffic - 96.73% of Merchant onboarding completed without any intervention from the support team for the Core Business in Fiscal 2026.
Diversified merchant base minimizing revenue concentration risk (qualitative factor listed in Basis for Offer Price).

Full transaction accountability enhancing merchant trust and retention - total compensation paid to Merchants of Rs.531.11 million in Fiscal 2026, which the Company states is recovered in full from logistics partners so that no net loss is absorbed; 344 Key Account Managers as of March 31, 2026.

AI, data and automation-driven platform for operational efficiency - data points derived from more than 155 million end consumers and more than 730 million unique transactions processed between October 2016 and March 2026.
Modular and open platform enabling rapid expansion - leverages services from more than 250 ecosystem partners from April 2021 to March 2026; open API integrations for third-party developers.

Risk of being unsuccessful in making, integrating and maintaining acquisitions and strategic investments, with failure to realise economic benefit potentially resulting in substantial impairment charges.

overview.business_model: Revenue is earned from merchant solutions built around shipping, fulfilment and conversion technology that connect retailers, carriers and end consumers domestically and cross-border. Options remain outstanding for 35,050,554 Equity Shares under ESOP 2016 and 27,584,466 Equity Shares under ESOP 2024, against pre-Offer capital of 636,278,384 Equity Shares.

ZERO of the Offer objects is committed. Risk Factor 3 states plainly: 'We have not entered into any definitive arrangements to utilize the Net Proceeds of the Offer.' No purchase order, no definitive agreement and no amount paid to any vendor is disclosed. The four quotations relied upon (Mantarav Private Limited and VUI Live Private Limited for marketing; Mantarav and Cloudkeeper India Private Limited for technology) carry NO printed amount and NO validity or expiry date, and the RHP adds that the Company 'may decide not to engage these service providers'. None of the objects has been appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency, and no amount is disclosed as already deployed.

The third object is entirely blank: 'Funding inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes' is printed as [●] for its amount, for each of Fiscal 2027, 2028 and 2029, and for the split between the two sub-heads — bounded only by the SEBI caps of 25% of Gross Proceeds individually and 35% combined. The Total row of the Objects table is likewise [●]. The RHP states 'we have not entered into any definitive agreements towards any future acquisitions or strategic initiatives' and names no target.

Courier concentration is at a three-year high in a business with no exclusivity: the top five active couriers carried 84.50% of total shipment volumes in FY26 against 83.33% (FY25) and 83.38% (FY24), out of 42 active courier partners, on contracts the RHP describes as non-exclusive independent-contractor arrangements terminable by either side. Cost of Merchant Solutions was 69.39% / 69.34% / 58.94% of Total Expenses (₹14,941.29 / 12,129.31 / 10,070.37 mn), top three vendors 41.48% / 44.59% / 39.40% and top ten vendors 55.24% / 57.85% / 50.93% of Total Expenses.

Goodwill of ₹9,153.15 mn is 36.54% of Total assets of ₹25,047.68 mn at March 31, 2026 (39.65% and 44.62% in the two prior years) against Net Worth of ₹15,242.89 mn, and this exact asset has already been written down: Fiscal 2024 exceptional items included impairment in value of Goodwill ₹1,767.42 mn (Shiprocket Omuni ₹1,246.41 mn, Swiftly/Wigzo ₹521.01 mn) and impairment of Intangible assets ₹753.15 mn. Other Intangible assets now stand at just ₹4.91 mn, 0.02% of total assets. The RHP itself notes that PFIC classification for U.S. holders 'depends largely on the expected value of its goodwill'.

The operating metrics that matter to the growth story deteriorated in Fiscal 2026 even as headline revenue rose 24%: Power Merchants – Core Business FELL from 9,242 to 8,815 (8,599 in FY24); total Power Merchants grew only 0.85% to 10,090 after 10.92% and 10.13%; new end consumers served FELL from 30.11 mn to 29.38 mn, so all growth in end consumers came from repeat users; Power Merchants using more than two products FELL to 75.48% from 78.68%, below the FY24 level of 77.14%; and new Active Merchants acquired through the Core Business fell from 93.77% to 88.98% to 79.02%. The RHP attributes the Core stall to 'Project Nexus', a restructuring of merchant acquisition and key account management.

The one cohort curve the RHP prints in text shows a cohort below its own starting volume in year three: the Fiscal 2023 Merchant cohort reached only 0.89x its initial-year unique transactions by Fiscal 2026 (the RHP attributes this to the Pickrr acquisition and integration), against 1.81x in year two for the Fiscal 2024 cohort and 1.93x in year one for the Fiscal 2025 cohort. No revenue-retention or net-revenue-retention percentage appears anywhere in the document.

Rule 11(g) audit-trail modifications appear in the statutory auditor's report for ALL THREE fiscals and remain unremediated: the audit trail (edit log) is not enabled for certain logs of deleted or changed transactions and is not enabled at the database level for the Company and its Subsidiaries; for Fiscal 2024 management was unable to comment on the database-level trail at all because the database is maintained by a third-party service provider. For Pickrr, which used Tally, the auditors record that the audit trail feature 'is not enabled' and that they 'are unable to assess whether the audit trail has been preserved as per statutory record retention requirements'. The remedy stated is only that the Company 'will be implementing the necessary system configurations'.

The share-based payment accounting has already failed once: the Fiscal 2024 emphasis of matter records an incorrect cost accrual for share-based expenses that forced restatement of the FY2023 statements and of the position as at April 1, 2022, increasing the Share Based Payment Reserve by ₹254.90 mn with a corresponding ₹254.90 mn impact in Retained Earnings and in Share Based Payment Expense. This sits alongside books-of-account modifications for FY2024 (Company: no daily backup on servers in India) and FY2025 (Pickrr: no daily India-located backup from April 1, 2024 to December 31, 2024).

There is no identifiable promoter and no promoter group, so Regulation 14(1) minimum promoters' contribution does not apply and NO Equity Shares are locked in for eighteen months; the entire pre-Offer capital is locked in for only six months under Regulation 17(1), with carve-outs for OFS shares, ESOP-scheme shares and VCF/Category I and II AIF holdings. Bertelsmann Nederland B.V. holds 21.32% and Eternal Limited 6.85% pre-Offer. The auditor-certified WACA for the Selling Shareholders is ₹38.99 for both the last one year and the last three years, over an acquisition-price range of Nil (bonus) to ₹163.14; founders Gautam Kapoor, Saahil Goel and Vishesh Khurana show a WACA of ₹0.28, ₹0.28 and ₹0.27 respectively, and Nil for shares acquired in the last one year.

The Company is a foreign owned and controlled company under the Consolidated FDI Policy and the FEMA Non-debt Instruments Rules, which restricts certain business activities and investments without prior Government approval and binds issues and transfers of Equity Shares to pricing guidelines.

Offer Price, Floor and Cap Price, the number of Fresh Issue and Offered Shares, dilution, post-Offer capital and shareholding, Net Proceeds, offer expenses, the 'Cap Price is X times WACA' multiple, the issuer's P/E, market capitalisation, EV/Revenue and EV/EBITDA are all [●]. The only P/E printed is the peer group's 47.75x, which is a single company (Unicommerce), so highest, lowest and average are identical. The RHP itself states the Offer Price 'would not be based on a benchmark with industry peers'. No valuation figure has been formed here.

red_flags: ZERO committed deployment for the Net Proceeds. Risk Factor 3: 'We have not entered into any definitive arrangements to utilize the Net Proceeds of the Offer.' No purchase order, no definitive agreement and no amount paid to any vendor is disclosed for any object; the four quotations obtained carry no printed amount and no validity or expiry date; and the RHP states the Company 'may decide not to engage these service providers'.

Rule 11(g) audit-trail modifications in the auditor's report for all three fiscals, still unremediated at the RHP date, including the auditors' statement that for Pickrr's Tally system they 'are unable to assess whether the audit trail has been preserved as per statutory record retention requirements' — the audit trail was never enabled in that software.

Share Based Payment Expense of ₹1,123.43 mn in Fiscal 2026 and ₹912.77 mn in Fiscal 2025 — each larger than that year's Restated Loss of ₹792.45 mn and ₹744.49 mn respectively — and the entire charge is added back in arriving at the 0.87% Adjusted EBITDA Margin the RHP leads with.

The Fiscal 2024 emphasis of matter records that share-based expenses were accrued incorrectly, forcing a restatement of the FY2023 accounts and the April 1, 2022 position, with a ₹254.90 mn adjustment to the Share Based Payment Reserve, Retained Earnings and Share Based Payment Expense — the same accounting area that now carries the single largest non-cash charge.

The loss widened in the most recent year: Restated Loss ₹792.45 mn (FY26) against ₹744.49 mn (FY25), on revenue up 24.03%, with EBITDA as printed negative in all three years — ₹(165.55) / (171.60) / (4,958.89) mn — and no EBITDA margin printed anywhere in the document.

Goodwill of ₹9,153.15 mn stands at 36.54% of total assets of ₹25,047.68 mn against Net Worth of ₹15,242.89 mn, in a company that already impaired ₹1,767.42 mn of goodwill and ₹753.15 mn of intangibles in Fiscal 2024 when acquired businesses fell short of their acquisition plans.

The third object — unidentified acquisitions plus general corporate purposes — is printed entirely as [●] for amount, sub-head split and every year of phasing, bounded only by the SEBI caps of 25% individually and 35% combined of Gross Proceeds, with no target named and no definitive agreement in place.

Courier concentration reached a three-year high of 84.50% of total shipment volumes in the top five partners out of 42, on contracts the RHP describes as non-exclusive and terminable by either side, while Cost of Merchant Solutions is 69.39% of Total Expenses.

15,931,538 Equity Shares (2.50%) are reported as pledged in the Regulation 31 pre-Offer shareholding pattern with no narrative anywhere in the document identifying pledgor, pledgee, obligation or release.

No identifiable promoter means no minimum promoters' contribution and no eighteen-month lock-in; the entire pre-Offer capital is locked for only six months under Regulation 17(1), with founders' WACA at ₹0.27–₹0.28 per Equity Share and a blended Selling Shareholder WACA of ₹38.99 after a 265:1 bonus issue made within the last twelve months.

Employee statutory dues were paid late in every disclosed fiscal, with delays running to 124 days (professional tax, FY25), 192 days (labour welfare fund, FY24), 201 days (TDS, FY24) and 346 days (professional tax, FY24).

The segment designated to receive the Net Proceeds is loss-making and its loss deepened: Adjusted EBITDA – Emerging Business ₹(1,689.89) mn in FY26 against ₹(1,499.05) mn in FY25, at a margin of (31.37)%.

Governance continuity broke immediately before filing: five directors ceased between December 23, 2024 and May 10, 2025 (three of them investor nominees resigning under the shareholders' agreement), all four Independent Directors were seated only in August 2024 or March 2025, and the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer role sat vacant for 24 days ending July 27, 2026.
strengths_observed: Revenue compounded through both disclosed step-ups while the Core Business segment turned profitable on the Company's own adjusted measure: Revenue from Operations ₹13,159.76 mn (FY24) to ₹16,320.12 mn (FY25) to ₹20,241.41 mn (FY26), the last two steps printed at +24.02% and +24.03%; Adjusted EBITDA – Core Business ₹721.73 / 1,569.33 / 1,866.37 mn; consolidated Adjusted EBITDA ₹(1,279.56) / 70.28 / 176.48 mn at Adjusted EBITDA Margins of (9.72)% / 0.43% / 0.87%. Fiscal columns are printed newest-first and were read in that order.

Merchant-side revenue concentration is genuinely low and has fallen every year: the top 10 Active Merchants contributed ₹2,135.97 / 2,373.60 / 2,466.99 mn = 16.23% (FY24), 14.54% (FY25) and 12.19% (FY26) of Revenue from Operations, the single largest Merchant 3.83% / 3.67% / 2.83%, and the Restated Consolidated Financial Information states that in each of the three years no single customer represented 10% or more of the Group's revenue from operations. 214,769 Active Merchants in FY26 (165,231 in FY25).

Operating cash flow moved from a large outflow to an inflow across the three fiscals: net cash from/(used in) operating activities ₹(2,159.92) mn (FY24), ₹18.97 mn (FY25), ₹526.37 mn (FY26). Note the RHP separately prints that 'net cash and cash equivalents for the purposes of the Statement of Cash Flows', after deducting the bank overdraft, remains negative at ₹(572.69) mn (FY26), ₹(1,182.25) mn (FY25) and ₹(1,289.79) mn (FY24).

Engagement and per-unit measures all rose across the three fiscals: Unique Transactions 132.28 / 164.35 / 202.08 mn; end consumers served under the Core Business 48.32 / 61.59 / 69.58 mn with a repeat rate of 46.79% / 51.11% / 57.78%; Power Merchant ARPU ₹1.28 / 1.44 / 1.78 mn (Core Business ₹1.12 / 1.28 / 1.54 mn); Revenue from Operations per employee ₹10.18 / 12.76 / 14.77 mn. Cumulatively, more than 155 million end consumers and more than 730 million unique transactions between October 2016 and March 2026.

The Emerging Business is scaling off a small base and its contribution margin has moved up: Emerging Business revenue ₹2,313.18 / 3,260.85 / 5,387.29 mn = 17.58% / 19.98% / 26.62% of Revenue from Operations; Contribution Margin – Emerging Business 1.47% / 9.47% / 10.55%. Within it, cargo and fulfilment ₹1,411.64 to ₹3,029.71 mn, cross-border ₹702.42 to ₹1,394.16 mn, ads and marketing ₹194.97 to ₹838.19 mn and others ₹4.15 to ₹125.23 mn over FY24 to FY26. New Active Merchants acquired through the Emerging Business rose 6.23% to 11.02% to 20.98%.

The balance sheet carries no term debt and the borrowings are collateralised by the Company's own deposits: Total Borrowings ₹2,132.75 / 2,446.65 / 2,420.12 mn (FY24/25/26), consisting solely of three overdrafts against fixed deposits with ICICI Bank (₹724.30 mn outstanding, FD rate + 0.50% p.a.), HDFC Bank (₹1,447.98 mn, term deposit rate + 0.25% p.a.) and Yes Bank (₹247.84 mn, FD rate + 0.30% p.a.); against these sit bank deposits of ₹4,275.88 mn (maturity beyond 12 months) and ₹2,049.44 mn (current) plus cash and cash equivalents of ₹1,847.43 mn. Net Worth ₹12,841.55 / 14,912.29 / 15,242.89 mn; NAV per Equity Share ₹21.63 / 23.44 / 23.96. The RHP states none of the borrowings as of March 31, 2026 contained restrictive covenants, no lender consent was required for the Offer, and there was no default in any of the three fiscals.

Contingent liabilities are Nil as of March 31, 2026 (Income tax — Nil under the Ind AS 37 summary), with capital commitments of ₹18.59 mn disclosed separately under note 33(a) — the RHP discloses no EPCG scheme and no export obligation anywhere in the document. The one historical TDS demand of ₹2.50 million (order dated March 30, 2022) was settled under Vivaad se Vishwas for ₹1.84 million, provided for in FY25 and paid on June 20, 2025.

Capital intensity is low and verifiable: gross additions to property, plant and equipment were 2.25% / 0.34% / 0.88% of Revenue from Operations across FY24 to FY26 (purchase of PPE including intangibles and capital advances ₹245.16 / 65.78 / 181.66 mn); the Company owns no delivery fleets and no fulfilment centres, operating instead through 42 active courier partners, 13 leased fulfilment centres of 762,826 sq ft across 10 cities, and more than 250 ecosystem partners integrated from April 2021 to March 2026.

The working-capital cycle is still float-positive: Cash Conversion Cycle of (35.71) days (FY24), (29.22) days (FY25) and (10.34) days (FY26) — negative in all three years, meaning payables run longer than the receivable base, though the advantage has narrowed sharply (see concerns).

Of the total Offer of ₹16,174.85 mn the Fresh Issue is the larger component at ₹8,855.00 mn, of which ₹2,100.00 mn has a fully identified, lender-named use (repayment/prepayment of the ICICI, HDFC and Yes Bank overdrafts), supported by a Statutory Auditor certificate dated July 27, 2026 on past utilisation of those loans. CARE Ratings Limited has been appointed Monitoring Agency under Regulation 41 (agreement dated August 3, 2026) with quarterly reporting to the Audit Committee until the Gross Proceeds are fully utilised.

Because the Offer proceeds under Regulation 6(2), not less than 75% of the Net Offer must be allotted to QIBs, with a full refund if that is not achieved — a structural check the RHP prints on the cover page.

Platform self-service and accuracy measures are quantified for Fiscal 2026 (no comparatives printed): 96.73% of Core Business Merchant onboarding completed without support-team intervention, EDD prediction accuracy 78.51%, RTO high-risk identification accuracy 83.01%, and 92.83% of shipping addresses pre-filled at checkout. Fastrr Checkout powered ₹65,998.25 mn of GMV across 13,173 Merchants; cross-border GMV was ₹5,081.54 mn across 5,884 Merchants. The Company states total compensation paid to Merchants of ₹531.11 mn in Fiscal 2026 was recovered in full from logistics partners.
